brief: META's negative free-cash-flow report and widening AI credit spreads (hyperscaler CDS, CoreWeave yields above 15%) drove a tech/AI-capex unwind: NDX fell over 3% and SPX 1.5%, while the equal-weighted SPX had its best relative day since July 2024 as money rotated into healthcare, consumer and utility names. Goldman flagged historic de-grossing: Fundamental L/S, Systematic and Multi-Strat books all fell more than 1% the same day for the first time since COVID, its HF Positioning Pair down 4.2% (worst since 2011), with zero offensive AI positioning. That selloff pulled Treasuries bid (10Y back below 5.00%), helped by a CTA short squeeze Goldman still sees room to extend, even as oil pushed toward $100 on Houthi and Strait of Hormuz attacks and a French sovereign crisis (10Y above 5.10%, CDS above 100bps, above Italian and US yields) added a second stress channel. Barclays expects Meta to tap credit markets again, weighing spreads; Goldman's Privorotsky called it reflexive: AI weakness eases issuance pressure and helps rates even as it hurts equities.
